description: API Can Code is an interest-driven high-school data-science curriculum developed by Rotem Israel-Fishelson and collaborators that uses public APIs, EduBlocks, and CODAP for authentic data exploration and communication.
title: API Can Code

description: APLUS is an online learning-by-teaching environment developed by its researchers in which students tutor the SimStudent virtual agent to solve algebraic equations through guided problem solving.
title: APLUS (Artificial Peer Learning Using SimStudent)

description: A researcher-developed calculus assessment by Mehmet Fatih Ocal comprising six open-ended questions that measure undergraduate students' conceptual and procedural knowledge of derivative applications.
title: Applications of Derivative Test (ADT)

description: A domain-general architecture and authoring framework by MacLellan and Koedinger for creating teachable-agent tutors with learner models that can be trained across diverse instructional domains.
title: Apprentice Learner Architecture

description: A course-specific 22-item self-report inventory developed by Trigwell and Prosser for measuring academics' teacher/content-focused and student/learning-focused approaches to teaching.
title: Approaches to Teaching Inventory-Revised (ATI-R)

description: A software environment developed by Walker et al.
title: APTA (Adaptive Peer Tutoring Assistant)

description: A standardized, culture-free school-readiness assessment developed by South Africa's Human Sciences Research Council, comprising subtests of perception, spatial ability, reasoning, numerical ability, gestalt, coordination, memory, and verbal expression.
title: Aptitude Test for School Beginners
